sections.direction: Module 2 is the ticket office on game day before doors (M1 is the Cap Room after). The arena is an instrument, not a backdrop: the drawn bowl renders only settled turnout; pre-lock it is dark, closed, or absent. Premium comes from place, one hero per state, and almost nothing else on screen - not from violet/Inter alone. 75/25 budget named exactly: B1 sellout/house fills (/play + /board), B2 Two Peaks (/board), B3 class results frame (/board), B4 synthesis close (/board) at full cinema; H1 lock settle -> doors about to open and H2 N5-vs-N1 counterfactual at ~40%. /play state-by-state feelings; reference objects mapped: sidebar -> desk rail (club, night pips, two books docked, PIN demoted), goal card -> accountability card (two books, never Maximize Revenue), stat row -> tonight's printed facts, result screen -> box score with TURNOUT as hero, arena panel -> the building as a fill readout, dials -> two physical instruments of unequal size, bell -> a world event. /board: headline -> evidence -> footnote rail on every frame; the per-night class results table is missing today. /teach: calm command, Director Rail, elapsed clock only. Full memo: DIRECTION.md.

sections.what-the-student-plays: Five nights of set-one-number-and-wait: a facts card, one big price dial anchored at the season-plan price ($24 of a $10-$120 range), a secondary event-spend stepper, a Night-4 upper-bowl toggle, and one dominant LOCK IT IN button behind a confirm guard. No pre-lock preview of any kind, confirmed absent on every night's screen ('No preview. Nothing on this screen tells you what tonight will make.'). Two non-summable books (CASH, RENEWALS) update in a compact header strip after each close. REVEAL/ADAPT/COUNTERFACTUAL/SYNTHESIS move to the class board with a stronger, more premium visual register (arena backdrop, one chart per frame, one punchline sentence) than the student's own device carries.
sections.biggest-failure: The just-closed night's result is buried below the fold behind the NEXT night's full pricing UI on the 1366x768 student viewport. Confirmed at Night1->2 (screens-kid-b/06-play-night1-RESULT.png viewport vs -FULL.png fullPage: 0 attendance / -$520,000 result card sits ~700px below the fold, hidden behind Night 2's fresh dial and its own LOCK IT IN button) and again at Night2->3 (09-play-night2-RESULT-FULL.png: a sellout with 1,208 turned away, likewise buried). This inverts the founder-preserved reference decision that 'the result is a separate, larger state than the decision' (VISUAL_REFERENCE_SPEC section 2). For a persona who reads little and acts on the first big number/button she sees, the experience->consequence->adaptation loop that is this lesson's entire spine can be played end to end without the student ever reading a single per-night result card on her own screen -- only the compact red/gold CASH and RENEWALS header numbers are guaranteed visible, which register as 'good/bad' but not 'why.'
sections.moment-by-moment-notes: Join flow is clean, one screen, one CTA. HOOK is ~259 words and Night 1's pre-lock screen adds ~170 more before the first LOCK IT IN (measured on raw text dumps) -- heavy for this persona, though the hero price figure and dial and CTA remain findable without reading, so the mechanic itself is operable. The recurring blue guidance paragraph explaining the season-plan anchor repeats verbatim every night; a skim-first reader who reads it once (or never) then habituates to skipping it, so the actual pricing rule is experienced as an unexplained pattern rather than a taught mechanic. Kid B's naive play (price near dial max Night 1 -> zero attendance -> overcorrect near dial floor Night 2 -> sellout with fans turned away -> repeat Night 1's exact price on Night 5, same card, same result: zero again) produced a real, attributable, replayable causal story -- but that story lived in result cards the persona would structurally miss per the biggest-failure above. The Night-4 bowl toggle (CLOSED/OPEN, $95,000 cost) is legible and operable without reading its caption -- a genuine strength. The end-of-PLAY five-row summary table (17-play-night5-RESULT-allnights.png) is the one screen in the whole PLAY phase a fast reader could parse in ten seconds and should be the template for every per-night result, not just the final one. Board frames in REVEAL/ADAPT/COUNTERFACTUAL/SYNTHESIS are visually strong and would likely carry this persona's engagement if she is watching the class screen, independent of her own device's flaws. This was a solo one-desk test session; the COUNTERFACTUAL 'did anybody charge less and make more' prompt has no positive cross-desk answer at n=1 -- NOT VERIFIED as a flaw at real class scale.
sections.required-repairs: (1) Reorder or resequence the per-night transition so the just-closed night's result renders as its own screen state fully inside the 1366x768 viewport before the next night's pricing dial and LOCK button become the dominant on-screen action -- currently the next decision sits above the previous consequence in scroll order, screens-kid-b/06-play-night1-RESULT.png vs -FULL.png. (2) Stop repeating the identical guidance paragraph verbatim every night; either compress after Night 1 or make it reference the student's own last result so a skim-first reader gets a second real chance to absorb the mechanic. (3) Use the end-of-play summary table's glanceable table format (17-play-night5-RESULT-allnights.png) as the design template for every individual night's result card, not only the final one. Not recommending changes to: the join flow, the single-hero-figure-plus-single-CTA pricing card structure, the blind-commitment discipline (verified absent preview on every pre-lock screen), the bowl toggle's legible state change, or the board's visual register in REVEAL/ADAPT/COUNTERFACTUAL/SYNTHESIS.

data.finding: For the casual/low-reading grade 5-6 student pairs-on-one-device persona, the current M2L1 Full House build should not ship to a real classroom as-is. Every per-night result card renders below the fold behind the next night's full pricing UI on a 1366x768 student viewport (confirmed at two consecutive night transitions), inverting the founder's own preserved reference decision that the consequence gets a separate, larger screen state than the decision. A fast, low-reading student can play all five nights end to end -- dial, LOCK IT IN, dial, LOCK IT IN -- without ever reading a single one of her own result cards, leaving the experience->consequence->adaptation loop that is this lesson's core promise dependent entirely on a compact header number and, later, the class board -- not on anything her own device reliably shows her at the moment it matters.

sections.defects: Highest severity first. (1) /teach at 1366x768 (design-target teacher viewport): the session-pacing controls (Advance / Open the doors / Release the Two Peaks / End session) are inconsistently below the fold with no sticky/fixed anchor and no scroll-to-top on phase change -- DOM-measured scrollY=269 immediately after a phase advance with bodyScrollHeight 1526 vs innerHeight 768; confirmed no position:sticky/fixed CSS for this panel and no scrollIntoView/scrollTo in teach/main.ts. Not a hard trap (scrolling reaches it) but a classroom-reliability friction risk since /teach paces the class. (2) Class scatter chart (ADAPT and COUNTERFACTUAL, both 4-desk and 12-desk runs): same-color, different-shape marks can render fully stacked into one unreadable compound glyph (orange N2 square exactly overlapping orange N4 diamond in ADAPT; a denser unreadable cluster in the 12-desk COUNTERFACTUAL page 1) -- undermines the board's own 'SAME colour and SAME shape' legend contract for that cluster. (3) /play at 1024x600 (first-contact/small-Chromebook shape): the lock control is 64px below the fold on Night 1 (DOM-measured top=664 in a 600px viewport); reachable by scrolling (not the old overflow:hidden trap) but not visible on arrival. (4, minor/informational) On /play at 1366x768, the just-settled night's box score is itself partially below the fold on the transition frame that opens the next night -- by design (immediate progression), noted so a later wave doesn't misread a '-settled' filename as a full result screen. One suspected defect (a teacher desk-tile reading 'Pairfinished') was investigated via live DOM read and ruled out as a textContent-concatenation false positive, not a real collision.
sections.not-verified: Whether a real teacher's own scroll behavior reproduces the exact 269px offset (the underlying facts -- no sticky CSS, no scroll JS, controls below fold at two captured states -- are verified independently of that number). Desks other than Desk 1 were not captured as named screenshots at every state (per the canonical-capture contract), though the arc requires their screens (auto-commit label, late-join 'covered' copy) to render correctly to proceed. Whether the marker-overlap defect recurs across other price seeds -- not swept this run. Visual/aesthetic premium-vs-serviceable judgment -- out of role scope by design. teach/index.html literal markup and Full House's reduced-motion CSS coverage -- inherited NOT VERIFIED from the surface inventory, not re-checked.

data.finding: /teach at 1366x768 (the design-target teacher viewport) has no sticky/fixed anchor for its session-pacing controls (PHASE chips, Advance, Open the doors, Release the Two Peaks, End session) and no scroll-management on phase change, so those controls are inconsistently below the fold depending on how much director-note text renders for a given beat -- confirmed by DOM measurement and by grep (no position:sticky/fixed rule for this panel in theme.css; no scrollIntoView/scrollTo call in teach/main.ts). This is not a hard trap, but it is real live-pacing friction on the surface CLAUDE.md names as where 'teacher paces phases' -- a teacher mid-class should not have to hunt for the button that advances the room.

sections.what-the-student-plays: SIMULATED KID / AGENT-PLAYTESTED. Full pass of M2L1 Full House on the real build (port 4405) as a grade 5-6 student who follows no sport, /play at 1366x768, board at 1920x1080, five nights + reveal + adapt + counterfactual + synthesis. What the kid plays: a blind price commitment on a real dial ($10-$120), a subordinate event-spend stepper, and a one-night upper-bowl option, against a printed card (day, visiting club, Draw x/100, TV) and a two-book scoreboard (CASH, RENEWALS) that cannot be summed. Chosen line: N1 $20 / N2 $30+$10k / N3 $40+$20k / N4 $38+$20k+bowl (sold out 22,200, 2,150 turned away) / N5 $28, ending $1,615,864 and 54%. The decision is genuine and blind (OBSERVED: 'No preview. Nothing on this screen tells you what tonight will make.'), the consequence is attributable, and the Night-3 turnout collapse and Night-4 sellout are real surprises. The game is fully playable with zero sports knowledge: every card carries a Draw number, a five-dot meter and at least one plain-English line naming the economic force.
sections.pull-rating: FUNCTIONAL for this persona — below the Track 101 bar for a module finale. Not WEAK: the mechanic is real, the constraint bites, two moments genuinely surprised, and the kid finished wanting one more round with a specific plan (hold near $30 on small nights and watch renewals). Not STRONG: the payoff of every loop renders below the fold on the design-target viewport, the surface is a ~610px text column inside a 1366px screen, the building the kid is supposedly running is never drawn (a 6px bar), turnout and renewal changes arrive with no reason line, and the kid's own desk is never named in front of the room.
sections.biggest-failure: OBSERVED — the consequence is below the fold and underneath the next decision. At 1366x768 each new night loads as card + dials + LOCK IT IN, with last night's result filed beneath the next choice; KEPT and the renewals change sit ~120-140px past the fold on Night 2 (kid-c-fold-viewport vs kid-c-fold-fullpage), the Night-3 collapse is entirely below it by Night 4, and the single theatrical beat in the whole student surface — FULL HOUSE / 22,200 of 22,200 / 2,150 could not get in — renders at y~760-890 (kid-c-sellout). The price dial also re-arms at the plan price $24 every night, so the screen is ready to take a click before the kid has been shown anything. For a student with no sports intuition, watching what happened last time is the only learning channel there is, and the layout hides it.
sections.moment-by-moment-notes: LOBBY: the rejoin PIN is the largest element on first contact; team identity is text only, but 'The biggest market in American sports. A lot of people, and a lot of them can pay.' is a working non-fan cue. HOOK: ~90 words of prose before any number; 'roster' in sentence one and 'season ticket / season plan / renewals' used throughout and never defined; the five-night slate with Draw numbers is behind a collapsed disclosure that sits below the fold (VERIFIED it stays open once clicked). PLAY N1: dial understood in seconds; the event-spend dial ('up to $120,000') has no visible purpose until a 100-word disclosure is opened; the knob overlaps the PLAN $24 label (kid-c-n1-decision). Locked-waiting is one sentence plus ~450px of black. N2-N3: results readable and arithmetic is plain (CAME x PRICE = TICKET MONEY), but each new night pushes the previous result further under the fold. N3 surprise: $40 on the biggest card so far drew only 68.2% and cash fell — no sentence on the result panel says why; the reason lives in a blue rule box further up. N4: card says demand will run past the building; sellout + 2,150 turned away + the honest 'last night's $20,000 bought nothing' verdict are the strongest writing in the product and both are below the fold (kid-c-sellout). N5: 'The only thing that has changed since Night 1 is you' lands. REVEAL: seven stages of the same scatter accumulating shapes, opening with 'this picture is NOT a demand curve' — a term not yet taught — and by stage 4 carrying a 6-line WNBA paragraph over a shrunken chart (kid-c-board-shock); no desk is named in any reveal stage, so the kid never sees their own five nights in front of the class. THE TWO PEAKS frame ('The cheaper ticket made more money') is clear and needs no sports knowledge. ADAPT: three numbered questions on a card — the worksheet moment (kid-c-adapt-worksheet); Q1 asks about a 'best price' the kid was never given. COUNTERFACTUAL: /play gives the one real answer to 'what would I do differently' via the channel split and WHAT IF lines (kid-c-play-cf), while the board names only desks that held the SAME price across the two identical cards — the desks that adapted, i.e. did what the lesson taught, are structurally excluded from the named class story (kid-c-board-cf). SYNTHESIS card 1 uses the room's own numbers and an outside-sports strip (flights on a Friday, movie tickets on Tuesday) that landed for this persona.
sections.required-repairs: Would move this persona (layout/copy/pacing only, no economics change): 1) render the night's result fully above the fold at 1366x768 and place it before the next decision, not under it; 2) give the sellout its own full-screen student beat instead of 120px of gold below a lock button; 3) add one reason line per book per night — why the crowd moved and why renewals moved — at the quality already achieved for event money; 4) draw the building as a bowl that lights up as it fills and resizes when the upper bowl opens, replacing the 6px bar; 5) define season ticket / season plan / renewals once in place, add one clause defining Draw next to the meter, and drop 'roster' from the hook's first sentence; 6) surface the event dial's one usable rule ('$100 is about 1 extra person tomorrow, nobody extra tonight') without a disclosure; 7) use the screen — a two-column desk instead of a 610px column inside 1366px shared by two kids; 8) give the locked-waiting state something to be; 9) add a named board group for desks whose price CHANGED between the two identical cards so adapting desks are not excluded from the only named moment in the debrief; 10) fix the dial knob overlapping the PLAN $24 label; 11) demote the projector's 'NOT a demand curve' and honesty disclaimers below the class picture. Would NOT change: blind commitment and the 'no preview' line; the Draw number + five-dot meter + plain line per card (this is what makes the lesson survive a non-fan — do not fictionalise the clubs to fix accessibility, it is already fixed); two books that never sum; the honest spend verdicts including 'bought nothing'; Night 5 replaying Night 1; the counterfactual channel split and WHAT IF lines; the outside-sports generalisation strip on the synthesis cards.

sections.what-the-student-plays: SIMULATED KID / AGENT-PLAYTESTED. Kid A (grade 5-6 NBA obsessive, Desk 1 New York Knicks, pairs on one 1366x768 device) played one full pass of M2L1 Full House on port 4403: LOBBY, HOOK, five nights, REVEAL x7, ADAPT, COUNTERFACTUAL, SYNTHESIS x6, COMPLETE, with 4 desks, a live teacher and a live projector. The mechanic: read a printed night card (day, visiting club's Draw 0-100, TV), drag one price slider between $10 and $120, optionally step a second unlabelled money dial, on Night 4 toggle an upper-bowl option, press LOCK IT IN, wait for the teacher's bell, repeat five times, then watch a teacher-paced board reveal. Kid A's line: $34 / $44 / $60 + $60,000 event money / $90 + bowl open / $34 on Night 1's repeated card. Ended $1,928,456 cash and 0% renewals. The blind commitment is real and produced genuine argument; the second dial was abandoned after the game's own copy said it is 'small either way, next to what your price does'. Two moments genuinely surprised: 7,810 people (39.4%) on the big-name Night 3, and 800 fewer people on Night 5 at the identical price. Both landed offscreen.
sections.pull-rating: WEAK for this persona. Not FUNCTIONAL: the loop's consequence stage does not reliably reach the student's eyes at the classroom's own viewport, and the student device is inert for the entire seven-stage reveal, so the experience -> consequence -> adaptation chain runs on parts the kid never sees. Not REFOUND: the underlying mechanic, the blind price, the two non-summable books, the Night-5-replays-Night-1 card and the Two Peaks class result are worth keeping intact; the failures are surface, staging and pacing, not foundation.
sections.biggest-failure: The consequence renders below the fold and nothing tells the pair to scroll. Measured at 1366x768 (the design target) immediately after the teacher rings the bell: night-result panel top = 758px, box score top = 813px, page height 1227px, scrollY = 0, no auto-scroll (31-fold-check-1366-after-bell.png). What fills the kid's screen at the moment of consequence is tomorrow's card and a price dial reset to $24 (09-play-n1-result.png viewport vs -full companion). The same defect eats the lesson's title event: Desk 3 sold out Night 4 with 6,525 turned away and the gold FULL HOUSE panel is cut in half by the bottom of the screen (19-desk3-n4-result.png). Asked whether the sellout felt like anything: no, because a pair that does not scroll never sees it. At 1024x600 the LOCK IT IN control itself is off the bottom (top = 664px in a 600px viewport, 30-play-1024x600-n1.png).
sections.moment-by-moment-notes: LOBBY: the largest, brightest object on first contact is a four-digit rejoin PIN; 'New York Knicks' is a name in a header with a generic crest and no club colour; two desks running the same club wear different crests (01-play-lobby.png, 01-board-lobby.png). HOOK: ~110 words of prose before any control (02-play-hook.png). NIGHT 1 pre-lock: the card reads well and Draw 22/100 prices fine without fandom, but the opponent is never a team ('a club that has lost four straight'), the PLAN $24 label overlaps the slider knob, the second dial has no label beside its number and its explanation is behind a disclosure triangle (03-play-n1-blind.png, 04-play-n1-spendrule-open.png). POST-LOCK: a ~60% empty waiting screen (07-play-n1-locked-wait.png). BELL: consequence below the fold, every night. RENEWALS: 50 -> 30 -> 10 -> 9 -> 18 -> 0 with no alarm state, same gold as CASH, no per-night explanation of why it moved; and on Night 4 the highest price of the season RAISED renewals nine points, contradicting the printed rule the student was given (11-play-n2-result.png, 17-play-n4-result.png, 20-play-n5-result.png). NIGHT 4: the card promises 'demand is going to run past what this building holds'; at $90 with the bowl open the desk finished 71.1% with 6,425 empty seats and a wasted $95,000, and no line explains the miss or grades the bowl bet. PLAY BOARD: an unlabelled scatter whose largest body text is a 40-word caveat about what the picture is not; no dot identifies my desk (15-board-n4-open.png). REVEAL: all eight student frames byte-identical, md5 05aa7a5185a8c10e1dcbde46ce5b736f, and THE TWO PEAKS is on the student device at stage 0 while the board still says 'waiting for your teacher' (22-play-reveal-s0.png, 23-play-reveal-s1..s7.png, 22-board-reveal-s0.png) - the punchline reaches the desks six stages before the room. Stages 1-5 are the same scatter with one more dot family each; stage 4 'THE SHOCK' shows nothing shocking (23-board-reveal-s4.png). COUNTERFACTUAL: the strongest student screen in the build - same price, 14,142 then 13,342, '-800 people, and that is renewals -800' (25-play-cf.png) - undercut by WHAT IF replay lines that read like a score I lost and contain sentences a 5th grader will not finish. SYNTHESIS: six projector cards of title-plus-paragraph with no computed visual, card 4 ~130 words, card 5 with six dollar figures, the same 'flights and hotels / bake sale in the rain' trailer reprinted under all six, pager wraps back to card 1; the student device shows one line, 'Look up at the board' (27-board-synth-p3.png, 26-play-synth.png). Copy defect a sports kid catches: 'On Night 3 in New York Knicks'. Nowhere on any of the three surfaces is there an arena, a court, a crowd, or a club colour. Zero page console errors observed.
sections.required-repairs: R1 BLOCKING - make the night result its own screen state that owns the viewport at 1366x768 and 1024x600 before tomorrow's dial is reachable; it must arrive, not sit under a fresh decision. R2 BLOCKING - the sellout (FULL HOUSE + turned-away count) must be inside the first screenful and legible on the board at the moment it belongs to. R3 BLOCKING - stop the Two Peaks spoiler reaching desks on PLAY exit, and give the student surface a per-stage reveal state that changes with the teacher's clicks (my night lighting up, my dot findable on the board) instead of eight identical frames. R4 HIGH - give renewals a felt state: an alarm treatment past a threshold, a per-night line saying in the pair's own numbers why it moved, an in-play consequence the kid can feel, and a printed rule that does not mispredict the student's own biggest result. R5 HIGH - make Night 4 escalate on all three surfaces, keep or explain the card's overflow promise, and give the $95,000 bowl bet its own verdict line. R6 HIGH - put the building on the screen: a drawn arena in club colour that encodes realized fill and lights on a sellout, on the student result and on the board. R7 MEDIUM - cut reading: hook to <=40 words, spend rule to one printed line with no disclosure triangle and no self-deprecating 'small either way', renewals rule to one line, board caveat out of the largest body slot, synthesis cards to headline + one computed visual + one takeaway, and print the beyond-sports trailer once. R8 MEDIUM - club identity: colour on the desk header and the dot, one crest per club, and an opponent with a record rather than only a role and a number, inside the no-desk-hosts-itself constraint. R9 LOW - open the price dial at last night's price, fix 'in New York Knicks', demote the rejoin PIN on first contact. WOULD NOT CHANGE: blind commitment with no preview of any kind; two books that never sum; no XP/badges/leaderboard; Night 5 replaying Night 1's card; Two Peaks computed from the class's own numbers; Draw printed 0-100 so a non-fan prices as well as a fan; teacher-paced stages with manual fallback; the Indiana Fever and San Francisco Giants facts (keep the content, change the delivery). NOT VERIFIED: any human student reaction; whether the Night-4 renewals rise is a model defect or a copy defect (Economic Truth's lane); projector fit beyond the captured frames; contrast/CVD; rejoin, refresh and mid-class restart.

data.finding: M2L1 Full House should not ship to a real grades 5-6 class as-is for the sports-fluent student. At the classroom's own 1366x768 viewport the night result renders at top=758px and the box score at top=813px with scrollY=0 and no auto-scroll, so the consequence of the pair's own decision is offscreen after every bell; the lesson's title event, the sellout, is cut off by the bottom of the screen; at 1024x600 the LOCK IT IN control itself is below the fold. Across the seven-stage teacher-paced reveal the student device is byte-identical in all eight captured frames (md5 05aa7a5185a8c10e1dcbde46ce5b736f) and already displays THE TWO PEAKS at stage 0, while the board still reads 'waiting for your teacher' - the lesson's punchline reaches every desk six stages before the room. Renewals fall 50% to 0% with no alarm state and no per-night explanation, and the printed renewals rule mispredicts the student's own largest result. The economics underneath is alive and worth keeping; the surface, staging and pacing currently prevent a real classroom from experiencing it. SIMULATED KID / AGENT-PLAYTESTED - not human-tested.
